summary: Subject prefix normalization strips tenant scoping, blocking cross-tenant impersonation in private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
A recent identity-proxy configuration/image change caused the 'sub' (subject) claim to be normalized by stripping tenant prefixes when the subject looks like an email address. For customers on Private deployments (customer: Finlytics) this removed tenant scoping from tokens issued during SSO/OIDC flows and caused RBAC checks and cross-tenant impersonation validation to fail.

Impact:
- Finlytics observed that service account impersonation and cross-tenant admin operations started returning 403s for ~30% of admin requests after a routine config sync on 2026-03-10.
- Affected operations: admin-console impersonation, service-account token exchange, and long-running automation that relies on tenant-scoped subject bindings.
- No tokens were accepted for impersonation; user interactive logins for non-admins were largely unaffected.

Environment:
- Customer: Finlytics (private deployment)
- Region: prod-us-east (us-east-1)
- Identity stack: Customer IdP (Okta) -> Redwood identity-proxy (private) -> Redwood auth-service -> RBAC sync
- Identity-proxy image: registry.redwood/identity-proxy:v1.12.0 (rolled out 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Exchange code with IdP and inspect id_token.
2) Observe 'sub' claim for affected users is returned as 'alice@example.com' instead of expected 'finlytics:alice@example.com' (tenant prefix missing).
3) Attempt impersonation with: curl -X POST https://private.finlytics.redwood/api/v1/impersonate -H "Authorization: Bearer <id_token>" -d '{"as":"service-account/ops-bot"}'
4) Observe 403 with body: {"error":"subject not in tenant scope"}.

Current behavior:
- Subject claim normalization removed tenant prefixes (pattern '<tenant>:<subject>') when subject matched an email regex. RBAC rules require the tenant prefix for tenant-scoped role bindings, so matches failed.

Expected behavior:
- Identity-proxy should preserve tenant scoping in the 'sub' claim unless explicitly configured to remove prefixes.

Initial workaround:
- Rolled back identity-proxy to registry.redwood/identity-proxy:v1.11.8 in Finlytics' private cluster at 2026-03-10 11:04 UTC; impersonation restored for most customers.
- Temporary customer-facing mitigation: instruct Finlytics to use service-account tokens (non-impersonation flow) for critical automation until fix is deployed.

investigation_notes: 03:40 UTC - Collected id_token samples from Finlytics: sub claim example before rollout: 'finlytics:alice@example.com' ; after v1.12.0 rollout: 'alice@example.com'.

Checked identity-proxy config: 'subject_prefix_handling' set to 'auto' at cluster level; PR #312 introduced 'auto' behavior which strips prefix on email-like subs unless 'preserve_prefix=true' is present. Private deployments were unintentionally inheriting 'auto' from base image config during config sync.

Auth-service RBAC matcher expects exact prefix match for tenant-scoped bindings (implementation note: match is string-equals on 'sub' when binding is tenant-scoped). No fallback logic present for missing prefixes.

Reproduced locally by running identity-proxy:v1.12.0 with test id_token containing sub='finlytics:alice@example.com'. Proxy returned sub='alice@example.com' downstream. Unit test coverage missing for subject normalization behavior across tenant-scoped tokens.

Reviewed related logs: identity-proxy audit log contains entries 'normalized sub from finlytics:alice@example.com to alice@example.com' at 03:14 UTC; correlation shows spike in RBAC 403s starting 03:16 UTC.
Found related customer ticket SUP-90315 referencing token prefix edge cases; cross-linked for follow-up compatibility checks.
resolution:
Immediate: Rolled back identity-proxy to v1.11.8 for Finlytics at 2026-03-10 11:04 UTC which restored tenant-scoped subjects and cleared the 403s.

Root cause: PR #312 introduced an 'auto' normalization mode that strips tenant prefixes for email-looking subject claims. The change was merged without gating it for private deployments; a configuration default caused private clusters to inherit the behavior. RBAC checks perform exact string-equals on the 'sub' claim and therefore failed when prefixes were removed.

Fix deployed: Auth team prepared hotfix PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/318 which reverts 'auto' behavior and adds an explicit 'preserve_prefix' config flag defaulting to true for private deployments. Hotfix was applied to image v1.12.1 and staged to canary on 2026-03-12; full rollout to private clusters scheduled after QA on 2026-03-13.

Post-deploy verification: Ran replay of Finlytics token test suite against v1.12.1 canary (all tenant-scoped impersonation flows passing).

Follow-up actions (owner in parens):
- Backport hotfix and release identity-proxy v1.12.1 with config default (Auth Eng - Diego Park).
- Add explicit integration tests that validate subject prefix preservation for private deployments (QA - Nivedita Rao).
- Update deployment gating so config sync does not alter 'subject_prefix_handling' unintentionally (Infra - Lena Ortiz).
- Add a canary dashboard for token normalization changes and an alert for sudden increases in impersonation 403s (Observability - Marcus Lin).
- Customer communication: Send RCA and timeline to Finlytics with SLA impact summary (Support - Aisha Raman).

Status: Hotfix merged and canary deployed; full private rollout pending scheduled maintenance window 2026-03-13 02:00-03:00 UTC.
